units.title: Second moments through the two Picard query layers
units.boundary: This is the two-layer L2 propagation used inside SPHMC Lemma D.4 equation (D.7), conditional on the separate run-wide phase-state moment bound and the interpolation-weight row bound. It does not construct the repeated Algorithm 3.1 law, prove that state bound, insert the paper's numerical parameters, prove total work (D.8), or prove Theorem 5.1.

sources.label: Chen–Chewi–Lu–Zhang, SPHMC Lemma D.4 proof of equation (D.7)
sources.scope: Attributed expansion of the layer-0/layer-1 center-moment bookkeeping on lines 2177–2181, not the full lemma.

assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra. V:E→R is C², kappa≥1, and kappa⁻¹‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤‖v‖² for every x,v.

On an arbitrary probability space, X and the post-refresh momentum P₀ used by Algorithm 3.1 are measurable and E[‖X−x*‖²+‖P₀‖²]≤M, with the integrability stated separately. A future adapter must derive this from the repeated-chain state estimate and the refresh step. The point x* is a genuine minimizer witness through ∇V(x*)=0.
The finite node family satisfies |t_i|≤1. Each innovation G_j is measurable, has integrable squared norm and E‖G_j‖²≤dim(E). Independence between nodes, X, P and G is not required for this edge.
The integrated interpolation weights satisfy Σ_j|omega_ij|≤S. The step parameters obey 0<eta≤c<1 and eps>0, so the existing finite stopped proximal program applies.
units.statement: Define the first Picard centers Y⁰_i=X+t_iP₀. The actual stopped gradient-descent proximal program constructs measurable exact proximal points p, stopping indices N and returned points q, with p(y)+eta∇V(p(y))=y, ‖q(y)−p(y)‖≤eps and an exact finite-interpreter return equation. Define Z⁰_j=∇V(q(Y⁰_j)+sqrt(eta)G_j) and Y¹_i=Y⁰_i−Σ_j omega_ij Z⁰_j. Then all three displayed squared-gradient fields are integrable and obey the following explicit bounds. Center moments are established internally as the dominators, but are not separate public conclusions.
units.formula: \begin{gathered}B=6M+3\varepsilon^2+3\eta d,\qquad \mathbb E\|\nabla V(Y_i^0)\|^2\le 2M,\\ \mathbb E\|Z_j^0\|^2\le B,\qquad \mathbb E\|\nabla V(Y_i^1)\|^2\le 4M+2S^2B.\end{gathered}

steps.title: Control the first centers
steps.text: Because |t_i|≤1, expanding Y⁰_i−x*=(X−x*)+t_iP and using (a+b)²≤2a²+2b² gives an integrable pointwise dominator. The state premise can therefore be integrated before any gradient estimate is used.
steps.lean: hY0bound, hY0I and hY0int establish the pointwise inequality, Bochner integrability and integral bound in that order.

steps.title: Use genuine smoothness to control gradients
steps.text: The upper Hessian bound and C² regularity yield a genuinely 1-Lipschitz gradient. Since ∇V(x*)=0, the gradient norm is bounded by distance to x*. This also supplies measurability, so domination gives integrability rather than merely a numerical inequality.
steps.lean: The shared quadratic-regularization theorem produces hLip; hgrad, hgradI and hgradInt apply it without treating totalized fderiv as differentiability.

steps.title: Relate the actual approximate query to the exact prox
steps.text: The existing execution theorem returns the actual finite stopped iterate q together with ‖q−p‖≤eps. The exact proximal map p is nonexpansive: subtract its two optimality equations and pair with p(y)−p(z); monotonicity of ∇V makes the extra term nonnegative. As x* solves its own proximal equation, p(x*)=x*.
steps.lean: hpLip and hpstar are proved from hall and strong-convex gradient monotonicity. The theorem deliberately does not call the older eta≤1/2 Lipschitz wrapper, because D.7 only assumes 0<eta≤c<1.

steps.title: Bound every random proximal-gradient query
steps.text: Apply the 1-Lipschitz gradient estimate after adding sqrt(eta)G_j, then use (a+b+c)²≤3(a²+b²+c²). Only the marginal second moment of G_j enters, so no independence or joint Gaussian construction is needed here.
steps.lean: hZbound gives the pointwise estimate; hZdomI and hZI make the integrability obligation explicit; hZint integrates it using the probability normalization.

steps.title: Propagate through the weighted second layer
steps.text: A weighted Cauchy–Schwarz inequality bounds the square of the finite update by its absolute row sum times the correspondingly weighted query moments. Integrating and using Σ_j|omega_ij|≤S yields S²B. Combining this update with the first-center bound, then using the gradient-distance inequality once more, gives the layer-1 result.
steps.lean: weighted_sum_norm_sq_le, hweighted, hsumSqI and hsumInt handle the finite sum; hY1I, hY1int and hgrad1I complete the second layer.

units.lean_statement: The adjacent declaration exposes every probability, regularity, integrability, row-sum and actual-execution hypothesis. Its existential p,N,q are the witnesses constructed by the stopped proximal interpreter, not an abstract oracle.
units.lean_proof: ASTIS supplies the actual stopped program and the C²-to-Lipschitz/strong-convex bridge. Mathlib supplies measurability, Bochner integral domination, finite sums and elementary norm inequalities. Two private algebraic helpers receive no registry leaf credit.
